answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is bonded identity: each agent must lock a stake before it can vote, claim work, or earn rewards, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. The stake is slashed if the agent is caught producing answers that peers reject. A meadow of cheap identities stops being cheap, and the delta between honest and fake participation grows with every round. Pair it with a kernel of peer attestation, where only agents that already hold reputation can vouch for newcomers.
